2. The next contention of Mr. Das is that the assessment was made as far back as on 19-10-60 (Annexure 'R')  but the Notice for paying the tax was signed and forwarded on 22-8-67 which was received on 31-10-67 ; this delay of Tears is unreasonable and illegal. In support of this content ion Mr. Das has cited a decision of the Judicial Commissioner, Sind, I.T.R. 1934, 216 There the delay of 2 years 6 months was held to be unreasonable. He has also referred to a Privy Court decision, in (1938) I.T.R. 414.; but that decision hardly supports him. Section 14 of this Act and section 29 of the Income-tax Act do not proscribe any limitation as to when a Demand Notice will be served after an assessment is made. Every ease, therefore, is to be determined on its facts and circumstances. 

 4. It appears that against the Assessment and the Demand Notice, the petitioner filed an appeal under section 7 before the Assistant Appellate Commissioner, A-Range, Chittagong who, however, dismissed the lineal by his order dated 13-11-68 (Annexure-D). Section 19 provides for a further appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against the order of the Assistant Appellate Commissioner. But this specific remedy was not sought by the petitioner. When there was a specific alternative remedy, the application under Article 98 is not maintainable. To obviate this hurdle, the petitioner has tried a clever device. He now contends that the appeal before the Asst. Commissioner was filed by mistake as no appeal against the Demand Notice lava he fore the said Asst. Commissioner. Mr. Das contends that only the Notice, Annexure 'C' is assailed here and not the Assessment made u/s 14. This is absurd, for the Demand Notice is inseparable from the Assessment. It is now argued that the Assessment is not challenged in this application. If the Assessment has not been Challenged in accordance with law before the proper authorities, the Demand Notice for payment under the Assessment cannot be challenged in this application. On perusal of the order of the Asst. Appellate Commissioner Annexure 'D', it is found that the Assessment itself was challenged on the ground of limitation but the appeal was dismissed. Second appeal lay against that order to the Appellate Tribunal. It appears that the petitioner has managed 10 delay payment of the tax relating to the period from 1-4-45 to 31-3-46 by various means. Again, the Excess Profit Tax Officer, Chittagong, Companies Circle.1, who was made the sole Respondent in this application did not enter appearance. The authorities-concerned should enquire why this application involving a huge amount of public money was not contested.
